purpose: Provide a machine-usable knowledge base of concrete marketing-strategy work-units (STP, value proposition, brand identity/equity, the 4 Ps, positioning, category design, moats, lifecycle) for planning, prioritizing, validating, and executing brand and marketing strategy as a subdomain node in a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Scope is marketing strategy and brand, not creative production, ad operations, or martech tooling.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable marketing-strategy work-units bounded to one heavy reasoning session.
All numeric values are heuristic priors; no observed dataset was supplied.
STP precedes the marketing mix, which precedes go-to-market synthesis and governance.
Both B2B and B2C marketing strategy are covered at the strategy grain.
exclusions: pricing accounting and revenue recognition mechanics

competency_questions.question: Given a business problem, what is the well-posed marketing objective (outcome, buyer, decision, horizon, metrics) it should be solved as?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKETING_OBJECTIVE_FRAME maps the problem to a measurable objective

competency_questions.question: Which segments exist in the market and how should they be defined and prioritized for the target?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: segmentation and targeting nodes produce a defined, ranked target

competency_questions.question: For the chosen target, what is the value proposition and why should this buyer choose this offer?
What is the brand's positioning: its frame of reference, target, key benefit, and points of difference/parity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POSITIONING_STATEMENT states one frame, one benefit, a credible difference

competency_questions.question: How is the brand differentiated from competitors and where is the defensible white space?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_POSITIONING_MAP locates white space on buyer attributes

competency_questions.question: What brand identity, messaging, and architecture express and protect the positioning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: identity, messaging, portfolio, and rebrand nodes express the position consistently

competency_questions.question: How is the message hierarchy translated into integrated communications across channels?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: messaging and promotion nodes carry one primary message across channels

competency_questions.question: How is brand equity and marketing impact measured and linked to commercial outcomes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: equity and measurement nodes tie brand health and marketing to outcomes

competency_questions.question: How are the four Ps (product, price, place, promotion) set to deliver the value proposition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: offer, pricing, channel, and promotion nodes form a coherent mix

competency_questions.question: What pricing and value-capture logic is consistent with the positioning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICING_STRATEGY justifies price by value and protects the position

competency_questions.question: Should the brand compete in an existing category or design a new one, and how?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CATEGORY_DESIGN decides and frames the category with an adoption path

competency_questions.question: What makes the position durable: which moats protect it and how imitable are they?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOAT_DEFENSIBILITY maps each moat to an imitation barrier and durability test

competency_questions.question: How does the strategy adapt to the product/market lifecycle stage and adoption curve?
How are the choices synthesized into a go-to-market plan, validated, and measured before commitment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GTM, validation, and measurement nodes synthesize and gate the strategy

glossary.definition: segmentation, targeting, and positioning: the core sequence that defines who to serve and how to be chosen
the mapping of target-buyer jobs, pains, and gains to the offer's relievers and creators stating why to choose it
the place the brand should occupy in the buyer's mind: frame of reference, target, key benefit, and difference
the attribute on which the brand is meaningfully and credibly distinct from competitors
the commercial value of buyer awareness, associations, perceived quality, and loyalty toward the brand
the hierarchy of core narrative, primary message, and proof points that keeps communications on-strategy
the four Ps (product, price, place, promotion) configured to deliver the value proposition to the target
naming and framing a market category and establishing the brand as its defining leader
a structural source of durable advantage (brand, network effects, switching costs, scale) that resists imitation
the firm's specific capability and asset advantage that makes a target segment winnable
the structure of relationships among master brand, sub-brands, and endorsements across a portfolio

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established marketing-strategy and brand literature (Kotler & Keller Marketing Management; Ries & Trout Positioning; Godin This Is Marketing; Aaker on brand equity; Osterwalder value proposition design; standard STP and 4Ps practice) and common marketing-strategy practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: observed market-share, conversion, or equity figures
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame the marketing problem as a well-posed objective: the business outcome sought, target buyer, decision to inform, time horizon, and success metrics, before any strategy or tactic is chosen.
contradictors: operator who runs tactics before fixing the objective

pros.claim: anchors every downstream choice to a measurable outcome
pros.example: tie a rebrand to a stated revenue-retention goal, not vanity reach

cons.claim: over-specifying the objective early can lock in the wrong buyer
cons.example: fixing a B2B objective when the real growth is prosumer

failure_modes: objective stated as activity (run ads) not outcome
metric chosen because it is easy to move
acceptance_tests: objective expressed as a measurable business outcome on a named buyer and horizon
success metric is causally tied to the objective

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: business goal or target buyer changes, or success metric is redefined

nodes.definition: Generate the buyer insight base: qualitative and quantitative research into buyer jobs, motivations, decision criteria, and perceptions that grounds segmentation, value, and positioning.
contradictors: marketer who substitutes assumptions for buyer research

pros.claim: grounded insight prevents strategy built on internal assumptions
pros.example: interview lost deals to learn the real decision criteria

cons.claim: research can be biased by sampling or leading questions
cons.example: a survey of current users that misses the rejecters

failure_modes: assuming buyer needs without research
biased sample drives the whole strategy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: research is unrepresentative or buyer decision criteria shift

nodes.definition: Partition the market into distinct, reachable, and economically meaningful segments using needs, behavior, value, and firmographic/demographic bases.
contradictors: marketer who treats the whole market as one segment

pros.claim: distinct reachable segments make targeting and positioning tractable
pros.example: split SMB by job-to-be-done, not just headcount

cons.claim: over-segmentation fragments budget and message
cons.example: 20 micro-segments no channel can address efficiently

failure_modes: segments overlap and are not distinct
segments are not reachable by any channel
bases chosen for convenience

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new buyer data shows segments are not distinct or not reachable

nodes.definition: Select and rank the segments to serve by attractiveness and the firm's right-to-win, committing scarce budget and capability to a defensible target.
contradictors: leader who chases every segment at once

pros.claim: focus concentrates budget where right-to-win is highest
pros.example: serve the underserved mid-market before fighting incumbents head-on

cons.claim: narrow targeting can cap growth if the segment is too small
cons.example: picking a niche that cannot fund the business

failure_modes: target chosen by size alone ignoring right-to-win
spreading budget thinly across all segments
acceptance_tests: target set tied to both attractiveness and a stated right-to-win
budget concentrated on prioritized segments

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a prioritized segment underperforms or a higher-value segment emerges

nodes.definition: Design the value proposition mapping target-segment jobs, pains, and gains to the offering's pain relievers and gain creators, stating why this buyer should choose this offer.
contradictors: team that lists features instead of buyer value

pros.claim: explicit jobs-to-gains fit prevents feature-led messaging
pros.example: frame value as 'cut close time in half', not 'has automation'

cons.claim: a value prop unvalidated with real buyers may be aspirational
cons.example: claiming a gain the offering cannot reliably deliver

failure_modes: value prop lists features not buyer outcomes
fit asserted without buyer evidence
acceptance_tests: value prop maps named buyer jobs/pains/gains to specific relievers/creators
fit statement validated against buyer language

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: buyers do not recognize the stated pains/gains or value-fit is rejected in testing

nodes.definition: Map competitors on the attributes buyers use to choose, locate white space, and define the differentiation that makes the brand the distinct choice on the dimensions that matter.
contradictors: analyst who differentiates on attributes buyers ignore

pros.claim: white space reveals a defensible, uncontested position
pros.example: find the unclaimed 'simple + premium' quadrant

cons.claim: perceptual axes chosen wrongly produce false white space
cons.example: white space exists because no buyer wants it

failure_modes: differentiation on attributes buyers do not weigh
map axes are not buyer choice drivers

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: competitor moves or buyer attribute weights change the perceptual map

nodes.definition: Establish the position: the chosen frame of reference (category), the target, the single key benefit, and the points of difference and parity that define how the brand should occupy a place in the buyer's mind.
contradictors: marketer who positions on many attributes at once

pros.claim: a single owned position is easier to remember and defend
pros.example: own 'the overnight one' rather than seven equal claims

cons.claim: a narrow position can become a ceiling as the market shifts
cons.example: a position tied to a shrinking use case

failure_modes: positioning claims many attributes diluting the difference
frame of reference is a category the buyer does not use
point of difference is not believable
acceptance_tests: positioning states one frame, one target, one key benefit, credible difference
points of parity neutralize competitor claims

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the chosen frame of reference no longer matches how buyers categorize the offer

nodes.definition: Define the brand identity system: name, purpose, personality, verbal and visual identity, and the consistency rules that make the brand recognizable across touchpoints.
contradictors: designer who styles before the position is set

pros.claim: a coherent identity system builds fast recognition
pros.example: consistent color and voice make the brand identifiable without the logo

cons.claim: identity rework is costly and semi-irreversible once in market
cons.example: a relaunch confuses an audience that learned the old marks

failure_modes: identity designed before positioning is fixed
inconsistent application erodes recognition

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: identity is inconsistent across touchpoints or no longer fits the position

nodes.definition: Build the messaging architecture: the core narrative, message hierarchy (primary/supporting proof points), and audience-specific variants that translate positioning into consistent claims.
contradictors: writer who improvises claims off-strategy

pros.claim: a message hierarchy keeps all communications on-strategy
pros.example: every channel leads with the same primary claim, varied by proof

cons.claim: rigid messaging can feel generic across very different audiences
cons.example: one claim that resonates with neither executives nor users

failure_modes: claims unsupported by proof points
messages contradict the positioning

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: messages drift from positioning or proof points are disproven

nodes.definition: Define and track brand equity: awareness, associations, perceived quality, and loyalty, with a measurement model linking brand health to commercial outcomes.
contradictors: marketer who equates equity with logo recall only

pros.claim: an equity model makes brand investment accountable
pros.example: link aided awareness lift to consideration and revenue

cons.claim: equity metrics can be gamed or lag real perception
cons.example: tracking awareness while preference quietly erodes

failure_modes: equity reduced to a single vanity metric
no link between equity and commercial outcome

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tracking shows equity diverging from commercial results or measure is invalid

nodes.definition: Decide the brand architecture: house-of-brands vs branded-house, sub-brand and endorsement relationships, and how multiple offers share or separate brand equity.
contradictors: team that launches sub-brands with no architecture logic

pros.claim: clear architecture lets offers share or shield equity deliberately
pros.example: an endorsed sub-brand borrows trust without diluting the master

cons.claim: architecture changes are disruptive and semi-irreversible
cons.example: renaming a portfolio strands accumulated equity

failure_modes: sub-brands proliferate with no architecture rule
equity diluted across confusing names

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: portfolio grows and the architecture causes equity dilution or confusion

nodes.definition: Shape the product/offer element of the mix: features, bundling, packaging, and the assortment that delivers the value proposition to the target.
contradictors: team that adds features unrelated to the value prop

pros.claim: an offer engineered to the value prop converts the position into product
pros.example: good-better-best ladders map willingness-to-pay to packages

cons.claim: offer changes ripple to pricing, ops, and channel
cons.example: a new bundle that the channel cannot fulfill

failure_modes: offer adds features the value prop does not require
bundle structure ignores willingness-to-pay

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the offer fails to deliver the promised value or assortment misfits the segment

nodes.definition: Set pricing strategy: pricing model, price level relative to value and competition, structure (tiers, discounts), and the value-capture logic consistent with positioning.
contradictors: operator who prices on cost-plus only

pros.claim: value-based pricing captures the differentiation as margin
pros.example: price to the WTP a premium position earns, not to cost

cons.claim: price changes are visible and hard to reverse with customers
cons.example: a cut that anchors buyers and is hard to walk back

failure_modes: price set by cost-plus ignoring value
discounting erodes the premium position
acceptance_tests: price level justified by buyer willingness-to-pay and positioning
discount policy does not contradict the premium claim

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: willingness-to-pay data or competitor pricing invalidates the price level

nodes.definition: Decide the place/channel strategy: routes to market, channel mix, coverage intensity, and partner roles that make the offer available to the target.
contradictors: team that picks channels by habit not buyer behavior

pros.claim: channels aligned to buyer behavior reduce friction to purchase
pros.example: sell where the segment already buys, not where it is cheap

cons.claim: channel commitments and conflicts are costly to unwind
cons.example: a direct push that alienates existing resellers

failure_modes: channel chosen for cost not buyer behavior
channel conflict between direct and partner

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: buyer purchasing behavior shifts or a channel becomes uneconomic

nodes.definition: Plan the promotion element: the integrated communications mix, channel/message allocation, and campaign architecture that delivers the message to the target efficiently.
contradictors: planner who buys reach with no message strategy

pros.claim: integrated comms make every channel reinforce one message
pros.example: paid, owned, and earned all carry the same primary claim

cons.claim: media allocation can chase cheap reach over qualified attention
cons.example: optimizing impressions while the right buyers never see it

failure_modes: channels carry inconsistent messages
budget chases reach not the target

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: channel performance or audience media behavior invalidates the allocation

nodes.definition: Decide whether to compete inside an existing category or design a new one: name the problem, frame the category, and position the brand as its defining leader.
contradictors: marketer who only optimizes within the given category

pros.claim: category creation lets the designer set the buyer's evaluation criteria
pros.example: name the problem so your offer is the obvious answer

cons.claim: creating a category is expensive, slow, and often fails
cons.example: educating a market that never reaches a tipping point

failure_modes: claiming a new category buyers do not recognize
category narrative untethered from a real problem
acceptance_tests: category frame is adopted by buyers or has a credible adoption path
category leadership thesis is defensible

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the market does not adopt the new category frame or an incumbent reframes it

nodes.definition: Identify and build the marketing-relevant moats (brand, network effects, switching costs, scale) that make the position durable against imitation and competition.
contradictors: operator who assumes a feature lead is a moat

pros.claim: a real moat turns a position into durable advantage
pros.example: brand and switching costs that outlast a feature copy

cons.claim: mistaking a temporary lead for a moat invites disruption
cons.example: betting durability on an easily imitated feature

failure_modes: calling an imitable feature a moat
no evidence the moat deters entry
acceptance_tests: each claimed moat is mapped to an imitation barrier and tested for durability
moat thesis survives a copy-this-tomorrow test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the assumed moat is imitated or proves not to deter competitors

nodes.definition: Adapt marketing strategy to the product/market lifecycle stage (introduction, growth, maturity, decline) and adoption curve, choosing stage-appropriate objectives and tactics.
contradictors: marketer who uses launch tactics in a mature market

pros.claim: stage-matched strategy avoids spending growth budget on a mature market
pros.example: shift from awareness to loyalty as the category matures

cons.claim: lifecycle stage is hard to diagnose and can mislead
cons.example: calling a category mature while it is still crossing the chasm

failure_modes: using introduction tactics in maturity
ignoring an approaching decline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lifecycle stage is misdiagnosed or the market transitions faster than planned

nodes.definition: Synthesize STP, brand, mix, and strategy choices into a coherent go-to-market plan: sequenced motions, budget, owners, and milestones that execute the strategy.
contradictors: planner who ships tactics with no strategic spine

pros.claim: a synthesized GTM keeps execution faithful to strategy
pros.example: every motion traces back to the positioning and target

cons.claim: a GTM plan can ossify and outlive the strategy it encoded
cons.example: executing last quarter's plan after the position changed

failure_modes: GTM motions disconnected from positioning
plan has no owners or milestones
acceptance_tests: every GTM motion traces to a strategy decision and a metric
plan has owners, budget, and milestones

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an upstream strategy element changes and the GTM plan no longer coheres

nodes.definition: Define how marketing impact is measured: the metric framework, attribution approach, and feedback loop that tests whether the strategy is working.
contradictors: operator who optimizes last-click only

pros.claim: a sound measurement loop turns strategy into a learning system
pros.example: incrementality tests separate real lift from correlation

cons.claim: attribution is error-prone and can institutionalize wrong decisions
cons.example: crediting brand demand to the last paid click

failure_modes: measuring last-click only
metrics not tied to the framed objective

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: attribution method misleads or the metric set rewards the wrong behavior

nodes.definition: Validate the marketing strategy before commitment: internal consistency across STP/brand/mix, evidence sufficiency, risk and reversibility review, and the human-review gate for irreversible or high-risk choices.
contradictors: operator who commits strategy without review

pros.claim: a governance gate stops incoherent or unvalidated strategy from launching
pros.example: block a rebrand commit until equity risk is reviewed

cons.claim: excessive governance can slow time-to-market
cons.example: review cycles that stall a time-sensitive launch

failure_modes: strategy committed without consistency check
irreversible choice approved without human review
acceptance_tests: STP, brand, mix, and strategy choices are mutually consistent
every high-risk or irreversible choice has a human-review decision record

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a validation check fails or a high-risk/irreversible choice lacks human review

nodes.definition: Manage a rebrand or repositioning as a controlled change: transition rationale, equity-migration plan, internal/external rollout, and rollback safeguards to protect accumulated brand equity.
contradictors: team that rebrands on a whim without equity analysis

pros.claim: a managed migration protects equity through the change
pros.example: carry the old mark in endorsement until the new one is learned

cons.claim: rebrands are highly irreversible and can destroy equity
cons.example: a relaunch that strands loyal customers and brand recall

failure_modes: rebranding without an equity baseline
no rollback path if the new position fails
acceptance_tests: rebrand has an equity baseline, migration plan, and rollback path
irreversible change has explicit human sign-off

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: equity tracking shows erosion during transition or the new position is rejected

edges.why_related: the framed objective scopes what buyer research must answer
edges.risk_of_conflict: researching with no decision wastes effort
edges.example: study buyers tied to the growth goal
edges.resolution_rule: fix the objective before scoping research

edges.why_related: the objective sets which market the segmentation must partition
edges.risk_of_conflict: segmenting the wrong market analyzes the wrong buyers
edges.example: segment the market named in the objective
edges.resolution_rule: frame the objective before segmenting

edges.why_related: buyer insight supplies the needs bases that make segments meaningful
edges.risk_of_conflict: segmenting without insight yields demographic-only cuts
edges.example: use job-to-be-done insight as a base
edges.resolution_rule: gather insight before fixing bases

edges.why_related: targeting selects among the defined segments
edges.risk_of_conflict: targeting before segments exist has nothing to rank
edges.example: rank segments by attractiveness and right-to-win
edges.resolution_rule: define segments before targeting

edges.why_related: the value proposition is designed for the chosen target
edges.risk_of_conflict: a value prop with no target serves no one
edges.example: design value for the prioritized segment
edges.resolution_rule: choose the target before designing value

edges.why_related: the value proposition defines which attributes the map should compare
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping irrelevant attributes finds false white space
edges.example: map competitors on value-relevant attributes
edges.resolution_rule: fix value before mapping competitors

edges.why_related: positioning selects the single key benefit from the value proposition
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning without a value prop has nothing to claim
edges.example: elevate one value-prop benefit as the difference
edges.resolution_rule: design value before positioning

edges.why_related: the white-space thesis shapes the chosen frame of reference
edges.risk_of_conflict: positioning into an occupied space invites parity wars
edges.example: position in the validated white space
edges.resolution_rule: map competitors before fixing the position

edges.why_related: the offer is engineered to deliver the value proposition
edges.risk_of_conflict: an offer not built to the value prop breaks the promise
edges.example: build the bundle that delivers the gains
edges.resolution_rule: fix the value prop before the offer

edges.why_related: pricing is set on the designed offer and its tiers
edges.risk_of_conflict: pricing before the offer prices a moving target
edges.example: price the ladder once it is defined
edges.resolution_rule: design the offer before pricing

edges.why_related: identity expresses the chosen position
edges.risk_of_conflict: designing identity before positioning styles the wrong idea
edges.example: design marks and voice to signal the position
edges.resolution_rule: fix positioning before identity

edges.why_related: the message hierarchy translates the positioning into claims
edges.risk_of_conflict: messaging without a position drifts off-strategy
edges.example: lead with the positioning's key benefit
edges.resolution_rule: fix positioning before messaging

edges.why_related: the identity defines the associations equity tracking should measure
edges.risk_of_conflict: tracking equity with no identity has nothing to test
edges.example: track the identity's distinctive assets
edges.resolution_rule: define identity before measuring equity

edges.why_related: the master identity anchors how the portfolio shares equity
edges.risk_of_conflict: a portfolio with no master identity confuses equity
edges.example: define endorsement against the master brand
edges.resolution_rule: fix master identity before portfolio rules

edges.why_related: promotion executes the message hierarchy across channels
edges.risk_of_conflict: promoting without a message house sends mixed claims
edges.example: every channel carries the primary message
edges.resolution_rule: fix messaging before promotion

edges.why_related: the channel strategy bounds where promotion can run
edges.risk_of_conflict: promoting in excluded channels wastes budget
edges.example: allocate media within chosen channels
edges.resolution_rule: fix channels before media allocation

edges.why_related: GTM sequencing depends on the pricing decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: a GTM with no price cannot model revenue
edges.example: sequence motions around the price tiers
edges.resolution_rule: fix pricing before GTM synthesis

edges.why_related: the GTM plan integrates the comms plan into motions
edges.risk_of_conflict: a GTM without comms has no demand engine
edges.example: fold the comms plan into the roadmap
edges.resolution_rule: fix promotion before GTM synthesis

edges.why_related: the GTM plan executes the positioning as its spine
edges.risk_of_conflict: a GTM disconnected from positioning ships random tactics
edges.example: trace every motion to the positioning
edges.resolution_rule: fix positioning before GTM

edges.why_related: the white-space thesis is the basis for a new category
edges.risk_of_conflict: a category with no white space fails adoption
edges.example: frame a category around validated white space
edges.resolution_rule: map competitors before category design

edges.why_related: the differentiation thesis is what the moat must protect
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming a moat with no differentiation is empty
edges.example: build barriers around the point of difference
edges.resolution_rule: fix differentiation before the moat

edges.why_related: measured brand equity is a candidate moat source
edges.risk_of_conflict: a brand moat with no equity data is unfounded
edges.example: treat tracked equity as a defensibility input
edges.resolution_rule: measure equity before claiming a brand moat

edges.why_related: the competitive landscape informs the stage diagnosis
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagnosing the stage without the landscape misleads
edges.example: read maturity from competitor signals
edges.resolution_rule: map competitors before diagnosing the stage

edges.why_related: measurement is designed around the GTM motions
edges.risk_of_conflict: a GTM with no measurement cannot learn
edges.example: instrument each motion against its metric
edges.resolution_rule: fix the GTM before designing measurement

edges.why_related: governance validates the synthesized strategy before commitment
edges.risk_of_conflict: committing a GTM with no validation risks rework
edges.example: gate the commit on the validation review
edges.resolution_rule: synthesize the GTM before validating it

edges.why_related: high-risk category bets must pass the governance gate
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated category bet can burn the budget
edges.example: require human review of the category investment
edges.resolution_rule: make the bet before validating it

edges.why_related: moat claims must be stress-tested in governance
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unvalidated moat overstates durability
edges.example: test the moat thesis in the review gate
edges.resolution_rule: claim the moat before validating it

edges.why_related: a repositioning is the trigger and input for managed change
edges.risk_of_conflict: changing brand with no new position is aimless
edges.example: drive the rebrand from the new positioning
edges.resolution_rule: fix the new position before the rebrand

edges.why_related: discount-driven pricing can contradict a premium position
edges.risk_of_conflict: discounting to hit volume erodes the premium claim
edges.example: a deep promo calendar undercuts a luxury position
edges.resolution_rule: positioning dominates: protect the premium; use structure, not list-price cuts

edges.why_related: narrow focus vs broad-reach growth pressure in GTM scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: broadening GTM reach dilutes the focused target
edges.example: expanding to all segments to hit a number breaks focus
edges.resolution_rule: targeting dominates unless validated capacity supports expansion

edges.why_related: long-term brand building vs short-term performance compete for budget
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-indexing on performance starves brand equity
edges.example: shifting all budget to last-click erodes brand over time
edges.resolution_rule: balance to a brand/performance split set by the objective horizon

edges.why_related: creating a new category vs exploiting the current stage pull oppositely
edges.risk_of_conflict: category education delays harvesting a maturing market
edges.example: evangelizing a new category while the current one is cash-generative
edges.resolution_rule: let stage diagnosis and right-to-win decide; do not do both half-way

edges.why_related: consistency of the existing identity vs the disruption of a rebrand conflict
edges.risk_of_conflict: a rebrand discards hard-won recognition
edges.example: refreshing marks customers already recognize
edges.resolution_rule: equity protection dominates: migrate, do not discard, unless equity is negative

edges.why_related: competitor parity points constrain which differences the value prop can own
edges.risk_of_conflict: claiming a matched difference is not a difference
edges.example: do not claim 'fastest' if a rival is equally fast
edges.resolution_rule: constraint: the value prop must avoid claimed-but-matched attributes

edges.why_related: channel margins constrain the feasible price level
edges.risk_of_conflict: a price leaving no channel margin kills distribution
edges.example: a price too low to fund reseller margin blocks the channel
edges.resolution_rule: constraint: price must preserve required channel economics

edges.why_related: validation can trigger a revisit of the positioning when consistency fails
edges.risk_of_conflict: an inconsistent strategy not revisited ships flawed
edges.example: a failed consistency check sends positioning back
edges.resolution_rule: revisit positioning on failed validation; stop when checks pass or max revisits hit

edges.why_related: measured results can trigger a revisit of the objective or its metrics
edges.risk_of_conflict: results that never feed back freeze a wrong objective
edges.example: a flat metric sends the objective back for review
edges.resolution_rule: revisit the objective when results contradict it; stop after one reframing per cycle

edges.why_related: performance by segment can trigger re-prioritization of targets
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring segment performance keeps funding losers
edges.example: an under-converting segment is de-prioritized next cycle
edges.resolution_rule: re-rank targets when segment results diverge; stop when ranking stabilizes

edges.why_related: a stable segment scheme should precede value design for anti-rework
edges.risk_of_conflict: reworking value after re-segmenting is wasteful
edges.example: finalize the segment scheme before designing value
edges.resolution_rule: sequence: complete and review segments before locking value

edges.why_related: identity and messaging are adjacent brand-expression artifacts to keep deduplicated
edges.risk_of_conflict: duplicating voice rules in two places causes drift
edges.example: keep voice in identity, claims in messaging
edges.resolution_rule: similarity: share the voice definition, do not duplicate it

conflict_axes.trigger: volume pressure pushes discounting that contradicts a premium position
resolution_order: capture value through structure not list-price cuts
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: positioning dominates: protect the premium; use bundling/tiers, not headline price cuts
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a standing promotion calendar is proposed for a luxury brand
conflict_axes.example: cutting list price erodes the premium claim and anchors buyers low

conflict_axes.trigger: budget pressure shifts spend from brand building to last-click performance
resolution_order: set a brand/performance split by objective horizon
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the objective horizon dominates: long horizons protect brand budget, short ones tilt to performance
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: all budget is moved to last-click demand
conflict_axes.example: starving brand for quarterly performance erodes future demand

conflict_axes.trigger: a growth target tempts broadening beyond the prioritized segment
resolution_order: confirm right-to-win in the focus segment
expand only when capacity and right-to-win extend
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: targeting dominates unless validated capacity and right-to-win support expansion
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the plan funds all segments to hit a number
conflict_axes.example: spreading reach thin dilutes the position and the budget

conflict_axes.trigger: resources are split between evangelizing a new category and harvesting the current one
resolution_order: diagnose lifecycle stage and adoption readiness
commit to create or exploit, not both half-way
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: stage diagnosis and right-to-win dominate: pick one bet deliberately
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: category education is funded while the current market is still growing fast
conflict_axes.example: half-funding category creation strands both bets

conflict_axes.trigger: a desire to refresh conflicts with the value of accumulated recognition
resolution_order: weigh renewal benefit against equity at risk
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: equity protection dominates: migrate rather than discard unless equity is negative
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a full relaunch is proposed for a well-recognized brand
conflict_axes.example: discarding recognized marks destroys hard-won equity

conflict_axes.trigger: the value prop wants to claim a benefit competitors already match
resolution_order: test each claimed difference against competitor parity
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: credible differentiation dominates: drop claims competitors equal
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: 'fastest' is claimed while a rival is equally fast
conflict_axes.example: claiming a matched attribute is not differentiation and invites rebuttal

conflict_axes.trigger: the desired price level leaves insufficient margin for required channels
resolution_order: set price to preserve channel economics or change route-to-market
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: channel viability constrains price unless a direct route replaces the channel
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a price too low to fund reseller margin is proposed
conflict_axes.example: a price that starves the channel blocks distribution

conflict_axes.trigger: a launch deadline pressures skipping consistency and risk validation
resolution_order: scale validation depth to risk and irreversibility
block irreversible commits until review passes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: validation dominates for high-risk or irreversible choices; speed allowed for low-risk reversible ones
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a rebrand commit is requested before equity-risk review
conflict_axes.example: shipping an unvalidated irreversible strategy risks costly rework

conflict_axes.trigger: timeline pressure tempts designing value on internal assumptions instead of research
resolution_order: require buyer evidence for value claims
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: buyer evidence dominates for high-risk value claims; assumptions allowed only as labeled hypotheses
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a value prop is locked with no buyer validation
conflict_axes.example: a value prop built on assumptions can be confidently wrong

edge_cases.trigger: positioning claims many attributes at once
edge_cases.failure_mode: a diluted position that buyers cannot recall
edge_cases.example: a positioning statement listing seven equal benefits
edge_cases.detection_method: count distinct attribute claims; require one primary key benefit
resolution: reduce to one frame and one key benefit

edge_cases.trigger: perceptual axes are not buyer choice drivers
edge_cases.failure_mode: differentiation on attributes no buyer weighs
edge_cases.example: claiming the 'simple + cheap' quadrant no buyer wants
edge_cases.detection_method: validate map axes against buyer attribute importance

edge_cases.example: a luxury brand runs a permanent discount
edge_cases.detection_method: check discount depth/frequency against the positioning's price tier
resolution: replace list cuts with structural value capture

edge_cases.trigger: value prop lists features not buyer outcomes
edge_cases.failure_mode: messaging and offer drift to feature-led
edge_cases.example: 'has automation' instead of 'cuts close time in half'
edge_cases.detection_method: scan value prop for buyer-outcome language vs feature lists
resolution: rewrite each claim as a buyer outcome

edge_cases.trigger: an imitable feature is called a moat
edge_cases.example: treating a copyable feature as a durable moat
edge_cases.detection_method: apply a copy-this-tomorrow test to each claimed moat
resolution: map remaining moats to real barriers

edge_cases.trigger: a new category is claimed buyers do not recognize
edge_cases.failure_mode: spend on educating a market that never tips
edge_cases.example: evangelizing a category with no adoption path
edge_cases.detection_method: require evidence of buyer recognition or a credible adoption path
resolution: pivot to positioning in an existing category

edge_cases.trigger: a prerequisite is modeled as a tradeoff
edge_cases.example: treating 'value before positioning' as a conflict not a dependency
edge_cases.detection_method: check that prerequisite relations are dependency edges, tradeoffs are conflict edges
resolution: reclassify the relation to the correct edge type

edge_cases.trigger: a dependent node is prioritized before its prerequisite
edge_cases.example: targeting ranked before segmentation is complete

edge_cases.trigger: a rebrand proceeds with no equity baseline or rollback
edge_cases.example: relaunching marks without measuring baseline equity
edge_cases.detection_method: require an equity baseline, migration plan, and rollback before any rebrand commit
resolution: block the commit pending baseline and rollback

edge_cases.trigger: impact is measured by last-click only
edge_cases.failure_mode: brand-driven demand is mis-credited, misallocating budget
edge_cases.example: crediting brand demand to the final paid click
edge_cases.detection_method: check the attribution model for incrementality vs last-click

edge_cases.trigger: a computed score or label is inconsistent with its formula or evidence
edge_cases.failure_mode: score-label mismatch undermines trust in the KB
edge_cases.example: a final_importance that does not match the node formula, or an observed label with no data
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived fields and re-check labels against evidence

edge_cases.trigger: a template placeholder or unresolved reference survives into the KB
edge_cases.failure_mode: placeholder leakage or broken reference fails validation
edge_cases.example: a leftover template token or an edge pointing to a missing node id
edge_cases.detection_method: scan for placeholder tokens and resolve all id references

workflow.objective: fix the marketing objective and build the buyer-insight base
acceptance_tests: objective stated as a measurable outcome on a named buyer and horizon
insight base grounded in buyer evidence
workflow.do_first_because: the objective and buyer insight are the highest-coupling foundation every later choice inherits

workflow.objective: define segments and select the prioritized target
acceptance_tests: segments are distinct and reachable
target tied to attractiveness and right-to-win
workflow.do_first_because: targeting is a prerequisite for value, positioning, channel, and the whole mix

workflow.objective: design the value proposition and lock the positioning
acceptance_tests: value prop maps jobs/pains/gains to relievers/creators
positioning states one frame, one benefit, a credible difference
workflow.do_first_because: positioning is the spine all brand, mix, and strategy choices must express

workflow.objective: build the brand identity, messaging, equity model, and architecture
acceptance_tests: identity and messaging express the positioning consistently
equity measurement links to commercial outcomes
workflow.do_first_because: the brand system encodes the position and is semi-irreversible once in market

workflow.objective: configure the four Ps to deliver the value proposition
acceptance_tests: offer delivers the promised value
price is justified by value and consistent with positioning
channels match buyer behavior
workflow.do_first_because: the mix operationalizes the value proposition and positioning into the offer buyers experience

workflow.objective: decide category stance, defensibility, and lifecycle adaptation
acceptance_tests: category bet has an adoption path
each moat maps to an imitation barrier
workflow.do_first_because: these high-risk, high-irreversibility bets must be settled before synthesis and governance

workflow.objective: synthesize STP, brand, mix, and strategy into a coherent GTM plan
acceptance_tests: every GTM motion traces to a strategy decision and a metric
plan has owners, budget, and milestones
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis must wait until the mix and strategy choices are stable to avoid re-planning

workflow.objective: design the measurement and attribution loop for the GTM
acceptance_tests: metrics tie to the framed objective
attribution uses incrementality not last-click only
workflow.do_first_because: measurement must be designed with the GTM so every motion is instrumented before launch

workflow.objective: validate consistency and risk, and gate high-risk/irreversible commitments
acceptance_tests: STP, brand, mix, and strategy are mutually consistent
every high-risk or irreversible choice has a human-review decision record
workflow.do_first_because: no irreversible or high-risk strategy may hard-lock before consistency, evidence, and human review pass

workflow.objective: manage any rebrand or repositioning as a controlled, reversible change
acceptance_tests: rebrand has an equity baseline, migration plan, and rollback path
irreversible change has explicit human sign-off
workflow.do_first_because: rebrands are highly irreversible and must run only after equity is baselined and governance passes

priority_rationale.notes: white space shapes position, category, moat
high-risk irreversible value capture before GTM
comms feed the GTM demand engine
semi-irreversible architecture follows identity and equity
closes the learning loop on the GTM
validation gate before any irreversible commit
most irreversible change runs last under governance

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk strategy is requested before validation completes
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk or irreversible marketing decisions require validation proportional to irreversibility before commitment
dominance_rules.required_action: block the commitment until STRATEGY_VALIDATION_GOVERNANCE passes
dominance_rules.example: refuse to launch a rebrand on an unvalidated deck

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is sequenced before an unmet prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: respect dependency precedence over raw value when ordering work
dominance_rules.example: do not design the offer before the value proposition

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric estimate is presented as more certain than its evidence supports
dominance_rules.rule: evidence labels and grounding dominate numeric precision; no observed label without observed data
dominance_rules.example: do not label a heuristic WTP estimate as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a strategy artifact is proposed for lock before acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.rule: QA and acceptance tests dominate the urge to lock
dominance_rules.required_action: run acceptance tests before any soft or hard lock
dominance_rules.example: do not hard-lock positioning before consistency checks pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible choice would be auto-approved
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for high-risk, irreversible, or evidence-weak choices
dominance_rules.required_action: route to a reviewer and record the decision
dominance_rules.example: require sign-off on a market-entry or rebrand commit

dominance_rules.trigger: a tactic contradicts the agreed positioning
dominance_rules.rule: the positioning dominates individual tactics that contradict it
dominance_rules.required_action: reject or rework the off-strategy tactic
dominance_rules.example: drop a discount promo that breaks the premium position

dominance_rules.trigger: a rebrand would discard accumulated equity
dominance_rules.rule: protecting brand equity dominates the appetite for renewal unless equity is negative
dominance_rules.required_action: migrate via endorsement rather than discard, with a rollback path
dominance_rules.example: carry the old mark until the new one is learned

dominance_rules.trigger: adding content would break schema or reference integrity
dominance_rules.rule: schema stability and reference integrity dominate added density
dominance_rules.required_action: fix references and structure before adding more nodes/edges
dominance_rules.example: do not add an edge to a node id that does not exist

dominance_rules.trigger: an object is created without source or competency-question linkage
dominance_rules.rule: traceability to sources and competency questions dominates unsupported object creation
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs and CQ links before accepting the object
dominance_rules.example: every node must reference SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR and a competency question

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker dependency to sequence or feedback
dominance_rules.example: do not make measurement a prerequisite of the objective it feeds back to

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the marketing objective before any segmentation, mix, or tactic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tactics run against the wrong objective are rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: media or creative work begins before the objective is framed
anti_rework_rules.example: buying ads before deciding what outcome they serve

anti_rework_rules.rule: ground the value proposition in buyer insight before locking it
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a value prop built on assumptions gets rejected and reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: value prop locked with no buyer evidence
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming a gain buyers never asked for

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete and review the segment scheme before locking the target
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: target chosen before segments are distinct

anti_rework_rules.rule: design the value proposition before fixing the positioning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: positioning with no value prop has nothing credible to claim
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: positioning statement written before value is defined
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming a benefit the offer cannot deliver

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the positioning before brand identity, messaging, and the mix
anti_rework_rules.rationale: identity, messaging, and mix built on a shifting position are rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: designing logos before the position is set
anti_rework_rules.example: pricing before the position's tier is decided

anti_rework_rules.rule: define the offer before setting its pricing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pricing a moving offer target forces re-pricing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: prices set before bundles are defined
anti_rework_rules.example: tiering a product that then changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: stabilize the mix and strategy choices before synthesizing the GTM plan
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a GTM built on an unstable mix must be re-planned
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: GTM drafted before pricing or category is settled
anti_rework_rules.example: sequencing motions around a price that then changes

anti_rework_rules.rule: run consistency and risk validation before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking an inconsistent strategy guarantees downstream rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a strategy hard-locked before consistency checks
anti_rework_rules.example: committing a plan that contradicts the positioning

anti_rework_rules.rule: obtain human review before any irreversible commitment
anti_rework_rules.rationale: irreversible commitments made without review cannot be cheaply undone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rebrand or market-entry committed with no sign-off
anti_rework_rules.example: relaunching marks with no rollback path

anti_rework_rules.rule: baseline brand equity before initiating a rebrand or repositioning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rebranding with no baseline cannot detect or reverse equity loss
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: rebrand started with no equity measurement
anti_rework_rules.example: no way to tell if the relaunch destroyed value

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or strategy review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defects sit at the top
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling or high-risk node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents and edges of the affected node
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change are listed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prioritized defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map the defect type to its repair subsystem
action: apply the fix via the formula script
acceptance_tests: each repair owned by one subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: node or edge base metrics changed
action: recompute all derived scores from formulas
acceptance_tests: all formula checks pass within tolerance

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator in dense mode
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a material score change occurs
acceptance_tests: posterior consistent with PI*EC

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk and irreversibility against thresholds
acceptance_tests: escalation has a recorded decision
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human decision recorded or risk accepted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare counts and checks against the prior version
action: compare object counts and pass rates
acceptance_tests: no mandatory check regressed

human_review_required_for: irreversible commitments (market entry, rebrand, category creation)
claiming a moat without a tested imitation barrier
pricing changes that affect the premium position
hard lock of the marketing strategy

positioning point of difference becomes parity
